subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should the Linux desktop client be admitted as a direct-local native UI client that can silently bootstrap a persistent operator-scoped device identity, once the compatibility and error-state repairs are made?
rationale: This changes the set of client identities eligible for automatic local pairing and operator-capable device credentials; source review can verify mechanics but cannot establish the intended long-term trust policy.

options.title: Approve the native trust class after repairs
options.body: Keep the Gateway-native design, fix the three identified compatibility/error paths, and retain explicit remote pairing.

options.title: Keep Linux on the existing transport
options.body: Do not expand native pairing admission until a separate owner-approved Linux trust design is available.

options.title: Require explicit local pairing
options.body: Use the native transport but require dashboard approval for Linux devices rather than silent direct-local pairing.

recommendation.title: Approve the native trust class after repairs
recommendation.body: Keep the Gateway-native design, fix the three identified compatibility/error paths, and retain explicit remote pairing.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the recent merged owner of Linux Quick Chat and authored the proposed native Gateway trust integration.
